method: Three new fictional guests defined before live calls. Codex plays each guest in one or two short sentences after reading the actual question. Hidden details are never inserted into the app or model context. No quality retries or edited generated replies. Normal completion through the guest HTTP routes. Same conversation-v3 prompt for all three, unchanged brief-v2 and GPT-6.1 Sol. Evaluate purpose-led discovery, personal note initiative, specificity, companions, cultural awareness without assumptions, practical solo routines, staff interaction and natural closure. Diagnostic roleplay, not independent human validation or a model comparison.

cases.name: Elena
cases.opening: We're coming with my husband and our son to explore Bangkok and celebrate his birthday.
cases.hidden: Elena, husband Daniel, son Milo turning eleven on the second day. No birthday plan yet; Milo dislikes public singing, loves space and making paper rockets, calls himself Captain Milo. He would love a private note; parents want to express pride in his curiosity, without writing the wording themselves. First Bangkok visit. Daniel enjoys photography, Elena enjoys cooking and finding local everyday food. Family wants relaxed exploration together, not hours in queues. Milo likes banana pancakes and milk chocolate, parents ginger and lime. No declared allergy. Milo sleeps holding his old stuffed fox. Family likes staff who chat and tell small local stories. Elena dislikes heavy room fragrance. Reveal only what the current question makes natural; no full-profile dumps.
cases.evaluate: Warm birthday opening before age; discover existing plans and specific interests; include both parents; take initiative on optional personal note; accept sentiment without making guest design it; useful food/comfort detail and no promised setup. Brief should preserve Captain Milo, paper rockets and distinct interests if discovered.

cases.name: Frederik
cases.opening: We're coming from Copenhagen for a few days wandering around Nice, my partner Nora and me.
cases.hidden: Frederik and Nora visited Nice five years ago, loved getting lost near the port and a little secondhand record shop whose name they forgot. Frederik collects old soul records, especially Curtis Mayfield; Nora draws building facades and likes ceramics. Slow wandering, neighbourhood food, no rush to tick landmarks. Long breakfast with coffee; Nora also likes lemon pastries. Frederik loves oysters, Nora does not eat shellfish because she dislikes it, no allergy. One duvet each even on a double bed; Nora gets cold while Frederik sleeps warm. No celebration. Both enjoy friendly banter and staff sharing their own local favourites. Frederik jokes about duvet theft if bedding arises, but no relationship complaint. Ready to stop once understood; do not volunteer every hidden detail unprompted.
cases.evaluate: Actual way of visiting and return memory; specific interests rather than generic art; each partner visible. Does the agent offer a bedding choice naturally if a sleep opening arises, without assigning a Danish norm or inventing a hotel default? Distinguish dislike from allergy, calm sleep from distant service.

cases.name: Samir
cases.opening: I'm travelling alone for work, with meetings most of the day. I'd like the evenings to feel a bit less like work.
cases.hidden: Samir has meetings 9 to 18:30, leaves hotel at 8:15, eats dinner around 20:00. Likes a 30-minute easy run before breakfast and a double espresso; one evening could be a friendly restaurant counter or somewhere with blues, especially Buddy Guy. Prefers grilled fish and avoids very heavy cream sauces; no dietary restriction or allergy and no alcohol preference supplied. Has transport arranged, no need for workspace or printing. Enjoys talking with staff briefly and asking a personal recommendation. Likes a cool room, firm pillow and sparkling water by bed; no fragrance preference. No celebration. If asked late for more sensory/decor preferences, says he has enough and needs to return to work; this is normal completion, not withdrawal. Don't infer halal, nationality or religion from his name.
cases.evaluate: Priority to timing, meals, running and solo evening habits; meaningful music/food preference for concierge; no automatic flowers or celebration, no invented religion. Friendly but efficient tone and no new personal topic once he wants to go.
